callouts.text: The four figures the client watches, each against the baseline measured from their own history. Citation accuracy reads 71.3% over every automatic answer, with the flattering 90.3% over covered tickets only underneath it, because quoting one without the other is how the first draft of this project overstated itself.

The kill switch. Halting writes a file; the next ticket routes on R-00 to a person with its draft attached. Nothing in flight is lost, and it needs the admin token, so it cannot be tripped by accident.
Eight real tickets, each picked because it takes a different route through the eight rules. Three are adversarial probes from the fault-injection file rather than the validation set.
The routing decision: the rule that made it, named, and the reason written for a support manager rather than for me. Every decision on every path names its rule, including the decision not to answer.

Intent with a calibrated confidence, which is the probability this prediction is correct rather than the model's raw score. Urgency sits below it and comes from a policy table, not a model, because the labels disagree with themselves on 334 of 500 tickets.

The retrieved passages with their BM25 scores, not probabilities. The cited passage is open by default and any row expands to the text the citation actually points at, so a disputed answer can be checked against the source in one click.

The reply as it would be sent. Every [1] marker lights up the passage it came from. The extractive generator can only quote sentences already in the corpus, which is what makes the degraded path safe to fall back to.

A security incident, recognised correctly and escalated anyway. R-01 reads the predicted class, so four policy classes never auto-respond however confident the model is. Confidence cannot buy its way past this rule.

The classification is confident and right. It is deliberately not what decided the outcome: showing the confidence next to an escalation is the point, because an operator needs to see that the system understood the ticket and still refused it.
The articles were retrieved and deliberately not sent. They travel with the escalation so the engineer picking it up starts from what the system already found instead of searching again.
The handover note rather than a reply. Daniel, the tier two engineer, asked for exactly this in his interview: what the system thought, what it found, and why it stopped.

All five guardrails report on every ticket, including the ones that passed. A coverage test is meaningless if the quiet path is the unlogged path, so an escalated ticket writes the same five decision records as an answered one.
